old: First-in-human trial of a bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor. Treatment-related hyperglycemia was low (4%) and not dose-limiting -- direct clinical confirmation that sparing mTORC2 avoids the metabolic toxicity seen with rapalogs/active-site inhibitors, while still achieving a 64% disease control rate.
new: First-in-human, open-label dose-escalation trial (n=57, advanced solid tumors, no comparator arm) of a bi-steric mTORC1-selective inhibitor. Treatment-related hyperglycemia was low (4%) and not dose-limiting, alongside a 64% disease control rate. Because the trial was uncontrolled and made no head-to-head comparison against rapamycin or an ATP-site inhibitor, this is encouraging early clinical evidence consistent with the hypothesis that sparing mTORC2 reduces metabolic toxicity -- it does not establish mTORC2 sparing as the cause.
why: Phase I, open-label, single-arm, n=57, no comparator: cannot support 'direct clinical confirmation' or a causal attribution to mTORC2 sparing.

old: 64% disease control rate; low (4%) treatment-related hyperglycemia confirming mTORC2 sparing
new: 64% disease control rate (uncontrolled); low (4%) treatment-related hyperglycemia, consistent with mTORC2 sparing
why: 'confirming' asserts causality from an uncontrolled trial.

old: A landmark RCT (n=89) - the first to prove rapamycin (sirolimus) treats a human lung disease.
new: A landmark placebo-controlled RCT (n=89) - the first to show that rapamycin (sirolimus) benefits a human lung disease.
why: 'prove' overstates a single n=89 RCT; 'show' is proportional to a randomised design.

old: Direct human proof that mTOR inhibition can halt a progressive disease.
new: Randomised human evidence that mTOR inhibition can suspend progression of this disease; the benefit did not persist after withdrawal.
why: 'proof' overstates; added the withdrawal caveat the study itself reports.

old: Because the cause here is direct mTOR overactivation, this is arguably the cleanest human proof that blocking mTOR works.
new: Because the underlying cause here is direct mTOR overactivation, this is arguably the cleanest randomised human evidence that blocking mTOR works in a genetically defined mTORopathy -- which does not extend to mTOR inhibition in people without such a mutation.
why: 'proof that blocking mTOR works' generalised beyond the trial population; scoped to the disease and design.

old: everolimus shrank tumor volume by 30%+ in three-quarters of patients.
new: everolimus shrank tumor volume by 30%+ in three-quarters of patients. Open-label and uncontrolled (n=28); randomised confirmation came later (FRA2013).
why: Uncontrolled Phase II result presented without design caveat.

old: Diabetic patients started on metformin had longer median survival than matched non-diabetic controls without the drug.
new: Diabetic patients started on metformin had longer median survival than matched non-diabetic controls without the drug. Retrospective and observational: consistent with a survival benefit, but confounding by indication and healthy-adherer effects cannot be excluded.
why: Large observational cohort framed in a way that invites a causal reading.

old: The definitive genetic 'dissection' of the two complexes in living mice.
new: The foundational genetic 'dissection' of the two complexes in living mice.
why: 'definitive' is an absolute claim; the substance (mouse genetics) is unchanged.

old: This cleanly assigned jobs to each complex and proved mLST8 is an mTORC2-specific requirement.
new: This cleanly assigned jobs to each complex and showed mLST8 is an mTORC2-specific requirement in mice.
why: 'proved' -> 'showed'; species scope added.

old: The definitive Nature review that put mTOR at the center of aging biology.
new: The landmark Nature review that put mTOR at the center of aging biology.
why: A narrative review (outside the evidence hierarchy) cannot be 'definitive'.

old: to settle a long debate: mTORC1's translational control runs almost entirely through the 4E-BP family
new: to address a long-standing debate: in these cells, mTORC1's translational control runs largely through the 4E-BP family
why: 'settle ... almost entirely' overstates one cell-line ribosome-profiling study.

old: Direct comparison of two long-term primate CR studies (NIA, Wisconsin) confirms health benefits; survival effect depended on study design.
new: Direct comparison of two long-term primate CR studies (NIA, Wisconsin) supports consistent health benefits; the survival effect depended on study design and control-diet composition.
why: 'confirms' overstates a post-hoc comparison of two non-harmonised cohorts.

old: demonstrated through integrated computational docking and in vitro experimental validation.
new: supported by computational docking and in vitro experiments in cell lines; no in vivo or human data.
why: In-silico + single cell-line work described as a demonstration.

old: causes macrophage immunosenescence and systemic aging by unleashing cGAS-STING paracrine inflammation
new: drives macrophage immunosenescence and systemic aging phenotypes in mice by unleashing cGAS-STING paracrine inflammation
why: Species scope added; 'systemic aging' narrowed to the measured phenotypes.

old: establishing the LKB1/AMPK/mTOR axis as a therapeutic target.
new: nominating the LKB1/AMPK/mTOR axis as a candidate therapeutic target in mice; no human data.
why: A mouse toxicology model cannot establish a therapeutic target.

old: imbalance causes replication stress.
new: imbalance drives replication stress in these cells.
why: Cell-line finding stated as an unscoped causal law.

old: Chronic rapamycin disrupts mTORC2 as well, causing insulin resistance;
new: In mice, chronic rapamycin also disrupts mTORC2, causing insulin resistance;
why: Species scope added: the mTORC2/insulin-resistance link is mouse data.

old: Chronic rapamycin causes insulin resistance
new: In mice, chronic rapamycin causes insulin resistance
why: Species scope added.

old: a small but essential cog that later proved especially critical for the mTORC2 complex.
new: a small but essential cog that later turned out to be especially critical for the mTORC2 complex.
why: 'proved' is absolute language for a biochemistry paper.

old: reversed that signature - a therapeutic proof-of-concept.
new: reversed that signature - a preclinical proof-of-concept in mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.
why: 'therapeutic proof-of-concept' read as clinical; scoped to preclinical.

old: - proof the registry finds real positive hits too, not only negative results.
new: - evidence that the registry surfaces real positive hits too, not only negative results.
why: 'proof' is absolute language.

old: Striking proof that mTOR inhibition doesn't just SLOW aging - it can partly REVERSE it.
new: Striking evidence that in mice mTOR inhibition doesn't just SLOW aging - it can partly reverse an established age-related phenotype.
why: 'proof' plus an unscoped generalisation from one mouse cardiac study.

old: supporting selective use.
new: supporting selective use. Retrospective and non-randomised, so treatment-selection bias cannot be excluded.
why: Observational cohort reported without a confounding caveat.

old: Genome sequencing of an exceptional everolimus responder pinpoints TSC1 loss as the sensitivity basis.
new: Genome sequencing of a single exceptional everolimus responder implicates TSC1 loss as the sensitivity basis. An n-of-1 observation, hypothesis-generating rather than confirmatory.
why: n-of-1 case described with 'pinpoints', which implies established causality.

old: mTOR kinase inhibition causes feedback-dependent biphasic AKT regulation
new: In cancer cell lines, mTOR kinase inhibition causes feedback-dependent biphasic AKT regulation
why: Species/system scope added to a causal claim from cell culture.

old: Muscle-specific raptor loss (not rictor) causes dystrophy,
new: In mice, muscle-specific raptor loss (not rictor) causes dystrophy,
why: Species scope added.

old: Raptor loss (not rictor) causes progressive muscular dystrophy
new: In mice, raptor loss (not rictor) causes progressive muscular dystrophy
why: Species scope added.

old: An activating MTOR mutation underlies an extraordinary clinical response to rapalog therapy.
new: An activating MTOR mutation is implicated in an extraordinary clinical response to rapalog therapy. Single-patient observation: hypothesis-generating, not evidence of a general response predictor.
why: n-of-1 exceptional-responder case stated as an established explanation.

old: identifying the mTOR-TFEB-GADD45alpha axis as a calcineurin-independent therapeutic target
new: nominating the mTOR-TFEB-GADD45alpha axis as a calcineurin-independent candidate therapeutic target (preclinical; no human data)
why: Mechanistic/in vitro work described as identifying a clinical therapeutic target.

old: a preclinical proof-of-concept in mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.
new: an early preclinical rationale from mouse models and cell lines, not a clinical result.
why: Removed 'proof' entirely rather than relying on a linter exemption.
